name: Nile Crest Medical Center
summary: A 220-bed hospital delivered turnkey — from operating-theatre air systems to a fully integrated BMS — while the outpatient block stayed open.
challenge: Eight operating theatres and twelve isolation rooms needed tightly controlled pressure cascades and 100% fresh-air handling units. The board also required a phased opening: the outpatient block had to treat patients while the inpatient tower was still under construction next door.
approach: Split the central plant into two independently commissioned loops so the outpatient block could run on its own chillers from month nine
Built a full-scale mock-up of one operating theatre to prove pressure, air-change and noise targets before installing the other seven
Coordinated MEP services in a federated BIM model, resolving 1,140 clashes before any sleeve was cast
Integrated medical-gas alarms, fire alarm and theatre HVAC status into one BMS front end for the facilities team
outcomes: Outpatient block opened on schedule while construction continued on the tower
All theatres passed third-party validation at first inspection
Handover two weeks ahead of the contractual date
Zero lost-time incidents across 1.3 million work hours

name: Orbit Business Park
summary: Three grade-A office towers sharing one central plant, designed to run 28% below the ASHRAE 90.1 energy baseline.
challenge: The developer was pre-leasing floors to multinational tenants with strict sustainability targets, and needed services that could be split per tenant without duplicating plant in every tower.
approach: Central chilled-water plant with variable-primary pumping serving all three towers
Tenant-ready risers with spare capacity and per-floor energy sub-metering
Demand-controlled ventilation driven by CO₂ sensors in meeting areas
BMS dashboards that bill chilled water and power per tenant automatically
outcomes: Energy use 28% below baseline in the first year of operation
Tenant fit-outs connected without shutting down neighbouring floors
Documentation package submitted for LEED Gold

name: Smart Village Data Hub
summary: A Tier III-designed colocation facility with 2N UPS topology and hot-aisle containment, now in final integrated systems testing.
challenge: The operator needed concurrent maintainability — any component of power or cooling can be taken offline without dropping a single rack — inside an existing shell building with limited roof space.
approach: 2N UPS and N+1 generators arranged so each data hall has two independent power paths
Hot-aisle containment with in-row cooling to fit the restricted roof plant area
Clean-agent suppression and very early smoke detection in every white space
Integrated systems testing with load banks simulating full IT load
outcomes: Level 4 commissioning completed for the first two data halls
Design PUE of 1.38 at full load
Final integrated systems test scheduled for Q2 2026

name: Shoreline Mall
summary: A 180-unit coastal mall connected to district cooling, delivered in an 11-month fast-track programme before the summer season.
challenge: The opening date was fixed by the summer season, and the coastal climate meant salt-laden air would attack exposed equipment within months.
approach: Connected to the city's district cooling network through a dedicated energy transfer station
Specified coated coils and marine-grade enclosures for all outdoor equipment
Ran tenant fit-out MEP in parallel with base-build through a dedicated tenant coordination team
outcomes: Opened on the fixed date with 92% of units trading
Single integrated fire alarm and voice evacuation across all retail zones

name: Olive Grove Residences
summary: Eighteen residential buildings delivered in four phases, each handed over with its own utility connections and snag-free MEP.
challenge: Buyers were moving into finished phases while later phases were still being built, so services had to be isolated per phase and every apartment had to pass inspection before key handover.
approach: Standardised apartment MEP layouts prefabricated as plumbing and electrical kits
Phase-by-phase utility connections with temporary isolation between live and construction zones
Digital snagging app so every defect was photographed, assigned and closed within 48 hours
outcomes: 1,240 apartments handed over across four phases
Average of 0.6 MEP snags per apartment at handover

name: Capital Gate International School
summary: A K-12 campus for 1,200 students, fully serviced in nine months so classes could start on the first day of the academic year.
challenge: The academic calendar fixed the deadline. Any delay to MEP would push 1,200 students into temporary classrooms for a full term.
approach: Zoned VRF with per-classroom control so empty rooms don't cool
Pre-assembled riser modules lifted into place to save four weeks on site
Campus-wide IP CCTV, access control and PA on one structured cabling backbone
Night-shift installation in completed blocks while day shifts continued structure works
outcomes: School opened on the first day of term
Classroom cooling energy 22% lower than the design estimate in year one

name: Delta Foods Processing Plant
summary: Process cooling, cold stores, compressed air and life-safety systems for a food-processing plant running three shifts a day.
challenge: Food-safety audits required hygienic, washable installations, and the client could not stop the existing production line while the new hall was connected.
approach: Stainless-steel and hygienic-grade installations in all production zones
Cold rooms down to −25 °C with redundant refrigeration circuits
Hot-tap connections to existing utilities so production never stopped
outcomes: New hall connected with zero hours of production downtime
Passed the client's food-safety audit at the first visit

name: Marsa Azure Resort
summary: A 320-key beach resort with its own desalination plant, six pools and guest rooms that stay quiet and cool through the desert summer.
challenge: The remote site had no reliable municipal water, and guest-room noise limits ruled out the usual rooftop condensing units next to villas.
approach: Reverse-osmosis desalination plant with storage for three days of peak demand
Central chilled water piped to villa clusters so no noisy equipment sits near guest rooms
Pool and water-feature plant rooms designed for salt-air durability
Treated grey water reused for landscape irrigation
outcomes: Guest-room noise below NR 30 across all room types
40% of irrigation demand met with recycled water
